**Archibald Prize** (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archibald_Prize)

The Archibald Prize is an Australian portraiture prize awarded annually by the Art Gallery of New South Wales (AGNSW), and is one of the most prestigious art awards in Australia. It is awarded to the best portrait, preferentially of some man or woman distinguished in art, letters, science or politics, painted by any artist resident in Australasia.

**History**

The prize was established in 1921 through a bequest of J. F. Archibald, the founder and long-time editor of The Bulletin magazine. It is awarded by the trustees of the AGNSW and is currently worth A$100,000 (the Packing Room Prize and the People's Choice are worth $1,500 and $1,500 respectively).

**Packing Room Prize**

The Packing Room Prize is awarded by the art gallery's packing room staff.

**People's Choice Award**

The People's Choice Award is voted by the public.
